futures.title: Futures
futures.lead: Binance USDT-M perpetuals and quarterlies: mark and index price, funding, open interest, positioning and live liquidations. All public, no key.
futures.liqHint: Binance's public stream, every pair. Totals accumulate while the tab is open.
futures.gl.mark.d: The contract's "fair" price, used by the exchange for unrealised PnL and liquidations. Derived from the index plus a smoothed funding premium, so a momentary spike in the order book can't liquidate you.
futures.gl.index.d: A volume-weighted average of the spot price across several exchanges: what the asset is "really" worth. The mark price gravitates around it.
futures.gl.funding.d: A periodic payment (every 8h) between longs and shorts that keeps the perpetual close to spot. Positive funding: longs pay shorts (the market is leveraged long). Negative: the reverse. Quoted per period; annualised = ×3×365.
futures.gl.oi.d: The value of every contract still open. It rises when new money enters positions and falls when they close or get liquidated. Rising price with rising OI = a trend with conviction behind it.
futures.gl.basis.d: The gap between a dated contract and the index. A positive basis (contango), annualised, is what the market pays to finance longs until delivery; it converges to zero at expiry.
futures.gl.liquidation.d: The forced close of a leveraged position once margin no longer covers the loss. A long liquidation executes as a sell (pushing price down), a short one as a buy. In cascades they move the market.
futures.gl.longshort.d: Accounts: share of traders net long vs net short. Top traders: the same, weighted by position size of the largest accounts. Taker: aggressive buy volume vs sell volume over the last hour.
futures.source: Data: Binance Futures (USDT-M), public endpoints, no key · chart: TradingView Lightweight Charts

legal.title: Legal notice & privacy
legal.lead: In plain words: who's behind this, what data we keep and why, and what is real versus what is a sample.
legal.who.title: Who's behind it
legal.who.text: MonsterBroker is a personal learning project by Álvaro Rodríguez Molina, open source on GitHub. It is not an investment services firm and is not supervised by any financial regulator.
legal.data.title: What we store
legal.data.text: If you create an account: your email, the name you choose, a hashed password (if you use one), the provider you sign in with (GitHub, Google, Microsoft or wallet), your wallet address if you link one, and the things you do in the app that count for quests and certificates (running a tick, opening the glossary). Also your quest claims, certificates and your review if you leave one. No banking data: no real money moves here.
legal.thirdParties.title: Third parties
legal.thirdParties.text: The database lives on Neon (Postgres, AWS servers in the US). Signing in with GitHub, Google or Microsoft gives us your email and name; we never see your password. Prices and candles come from Binance, CoinGecko, DefiLlama and alternative.me; those requests carry none of your data. Verification emails go through Resend or SMTP, depending on configuration.
legal.cookies.title: Cookies
legal.cookies.text: One ten-minute technical cookie during sign-in with GitHub, Google or Microsoft. Your session, theme and language live in your browser's local storage. No advertising cookies, no trackers.
legal.rights.title: Your rights
legal.rights.text: You can ask for a copy of your data or have your account deleted via GitHub or alvrich.vercel.app. Deleting it removes your events, claims, certificates and review.
legal.reviews.title: Reviews
legal.reviews.text: Published reviews come from registered members, under the name they chose, and an admin checks them before they show. Until there are at least three real ones, the home page shows cards marked “Sample”: illustrative texts written by us, not real people, removed as genuine reviews arrive. Usage numbers (accounts, ticks, quests, certificates) come straight from the database.
legal.certificates.title: Certificates
legal.certificates.text: Certificates attest that you did something specific inside the app. They are not an official qualification and don't equal formal training. Each has a public code anyone can verify here.
legal.web3.title: Token, badges and NFTs
legal.web3.text: MonsterCoin (MBK), the badges and the NFT certificates live on a test network (Base Sepolia). They have no monetary value, are not sold and cannot be exchanged for money. If anything ever moves to a main network, we'll announce it, after a legal review.
legal.disclaimer.title: None of this is financial advice
legal.disclaimer.text: The bot trades simulated money and the strategies are learning material. Whatever you do with your money on a real exchange is your decision and your responsibility.
